authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2757 kaphoṇi gives Hindi kohni/kehunī, Bengali kanui and Western Pahari khunni “elbow”. Simple contracted q/k and vowel variants preserve this historical elbow family. Reviewed comparison: MagahiNepal kūhnī “elbow” (f_v6vnecujnkkgw). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8857 prastara explicitly gives Prakrit patthara and regional pathar/pathara “stone”, including known cross-IA loans. Unaspirated patar remains a qualified phonetic variant within this identifiable stone family. Reviewed comparison: Hajong patʰar “stone” (f_wirpkzig3opp4). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: RathwiBareli mari “kill” (f_wzylsdq2mt5mq). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed. Reviewed comparison: Buksa dekʰa “he sees; he saw” (f_uzispb5iudogm). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
